Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "please make this into a practical inventory briefing for our food cooperative, Morrow Market, from the notes below. We did the closing count on Monday, November 11, 2024, in the receiving room and sales areas, and the system figures are the figures at that same closing, before anyone makes Tuesday adjustments. The briefing is for the shift leads who have to reconcile the count and plan Wednesday receiving, not for members or customers. Keep the units beside every count, and make it easy to tell what was physically counted, what the system says, and what still has to be checked. Don't combine anything that's expected later with the stock we actually had on Monday. We have a short staff huddle Tuesday at 8:30 a.m., and the leads need something they can use without looking through the whole notebook.

The dry-goods count is mostly in shelf units, not cases. Rolled oats are 25-pound bags: the system says 22 and the team counted 18 on the shelf plus four unopened bags in the reserve rack. The reorder point for oats is 16 bags. Brown rice is 10-pound bags: the system says 14; there were 12 saleable bags on the shelf, one saleable bag in the reserve rack, and one torn bag set beside the scale. The brown-rice reorder point is 10 saleable bags. The torn bag is not saleable stock and needs to stay apart from the count of usable rice. Canned tomatoes are 28-ounce cans, system 36, physical count 31, reorder point 24. Lentils are 5-pound bags, system 10, physical count eight, reorder point eight. Please show the different unit sizes as written; don't turn bags into pounds or cans into cases, because the leads compare the table with shelf labels.

For the chilled and frozen areas, apples are counted by case in the walk-in: system nine cases, count seven, reorder point six cases. Plain yogurt is individual cups in the front cooler: system 48 cups, count 42, reorder point 36 cups. Frozen berries are 12-pound cases in the freezer: system 12 cases, count 11, reorder point eight cases. One of the volunteers, Mara, said, “I put the damaged bag beside the scale so nobody would stock it.” The shift lead wrote next to it, “please leave it off the shelf until I check the seal.” Keep those as ordinary notes attributed to the people who said them; the lead has not reported a decision about whether to discard the bag. Don't turn either note into an approval or a final disposition.

There are two incoming deliveries to keep separate from Monday's count. Green Route Produce has a purchase order for six more cases of apples, scheduled for Wednesday, November 13, by noon. The order is scheduled, but the cases aren't here yet. A dairy purchase order for 24 individual yogurt cups is for Wednesday too and is still awaiting the distributor's confirmation. The receiving log doesn't give a delivery time for the yogurt if it is confirmed. Don't fill that gap by guessing or count either order as current stock. The apple cases matter for the Wednesday walk-in space, and the yogurt confirmation matters for the front-cooler reset and staffing, so mention the distinction in the planning part.

There is a specific if/otherwise instruction from Nina, the receiving coordinator, and I need both branches stated clearly. If the dairy distributor confirms by 10:00 a.m. Wednesday that the yogurt truck will arrive by 11:30 a.m., reserve two volunteers for unloading and clear two shelves in the front cooler. If there is no confirmation by 10:00 a.m. Wednesday, do not clear those shelves; call the distributor at 10:15 a.m. and leave the cooler reset off the Wednesday assignments. This is a real decision point, not a general suggestion to check in. Keep the deadline, arrival condition, and different actions attached to the correct branch. The separate six-case apple delivery is still scheduled by noon; it doesn't change the yogurt condition.

For the count summary, compare physical saleable stock with the system amount, while showing the damaged rice bag separately rather than silently adding it to usable stock. State any difference plainly, and don't guess why a difference occurred. Use the provided reorder points only: flag an item for a restock discussion when its saleable count is at or below its reorder point, but don't choose an order quantity or say that an order has been approved. The leads may decide what to order after they check the counts. Keep the incoming apple and yogurt quantities in a separate section or clearly separate column, and label them as expected or awaiting confirmation as appropriate.

Please include a numbered section in the briefing for the lead's follow-up, with the count reconciliation, the items at or below their reorder points, and the Wednesday receiving decisions. It should distinguish what can be acted on now from the dairy branch that cannot be settled until the stated confirmation deadline. The notes do not say who will call the distributor, who will verify the rice seal, or whether the delivery quantities will change, so don't assign those tasks to a named person or make up a new condition. If an item is above its reorder point, don't describe it as below threshold just to make the list longer. Use a calm internal tone, not a warning to customers, and keep the briefing compact enough for the huddle while including all figures and the relevant context.

At the end, add a substantive closing paragraph for the shift leads that brings together the Monday count, the open rice check, the threshold-based restock discussion, and the two distinct Wednesday delivery situations. It should remind them that the yogurt action depends on the exact confirmation condition and that the apple order remains scheduled separately, without suggesting either delivery has already arrived. Do not add a recommendation, a final approval, or a conclusion about the damaged bag; the purpose is to give the leads a clear, accurate briefing for their own follow-up.", "output": "Prepare a practical internal inventory briefing for the shift leads at Morrow Market food cooperative. Use the notes below to support Tuesday’s 8:30 a.m. huddle and plan Wednesday receiving. The inventory was counted at closing on Monday, November 11, 2024; the system figures are also from that closing, before Tuesday adjustments. Keep units beside every count and distinguish physical stock, system totals, and incoming orders. Do not include expected deliveries in Monday’s on-hand stock.

### Monday closing count

| Item and location | System amount | Physical count | Reorder point |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Rolled oats, 25-pound bags, dry goods | 22 bags | 18 on the shelf and 4 unopened in the reserve rack | 16 bags |
| Brown rice, 10-pound bags, dry goods | 14 bags | 12 saleable on the shelf, 1 saleable in the reserve rack, and 1 torn bag beside the scale | 10 saleable bags |
| Canned tomatoes, 28-ounce cans, dry goods | 36 cans | 31 cans | 24 cans |
| Lentils, 5-pound bags, dry goods | 10 bags | 8 bags | 8 bags |
| Apples, walk-in | 9 cases | 7 cases | 6 cases |
| Plain yogurt, front cooler | 48 cups | 42 cups | 36 cups |
| Frozen berries, freezer | 12 cases of 12 pounds each | 11 cases | 8 cases |

Compare saleable physical stock with the system amount and state any difference plainly. Show the torn rice bag separately; it is not saleable stock and must not be silently included as usable rice. Do not guess why any count differs. Preserve the listed units; do not convert bags to pounds or cans to cases. Flag an item for a restock discussion only when its saleable count is at or below the provided reorder point. Do not specify an order quantity or indicate that an order has been approved.

Mara, a volunteer, said, “I put the damaged bag beside the scale so nobody would stock it.” The shift lead wrote, “please leave it off the shelf until I check the seal.” Attribute both notes to their speakers. The lead has not reported a decision about whether to discard the bag, so do not state or imply a final disposition or approval.

### Incoming deliveries and Wednesday decision

Keep incoming quantities separate from Monday’s stock:

- Green Route Produce has an order for 6 cases of apples scheduled for Wednesday, November 13, by noon. The cases have not arrived.
- A dairy order for 24 individual yogurt cups is also for Wednesday, but is awaiting distributor confirmation. No delivery time is recorded if it is confirmed.

Do not guess the yogurt delivery time or count either order as current stock. The apple cases affect Wednesday walk-in space; yogurt confirmation affects the front-cooler reset and staffing. Keep these delivery situations distinct.

Apply Nina, the receiving coordinator’s, instruction with both branches and their conditions intact:

1. **If** the dairy distributor confirms by 10:00 a.m. Wednesday that the yogurt truck will arrive by 11:30 a.m., reserve two volunteers for unloading and clear two shelves in the front cooler.
2. **If there is no confirmation by 10:00 a.m. Wednesday,** do not clear those shelves; call the distributor at 10:15 a.m. and leave the cooler reset off the Wednesday assignments.

This is a specific decision point, not a general suggestion to check in. Keep the deadline, arrival condition, and actions attached to the correct branch. The six-case apple delivery remains scheduled by noon and does not change the yogurt condition.

Include a numbered follow-up section covering count reconciliation, items at or below their reorder points, and Wednesday receiving decisions. Separate actions that can be taken now from the dairy decision that depends on confirmation by the stated deadline. The notes do not identify who will call the distributor or verify the rice seal, and they do not say whether delivery quantities will change; do not assign these tasks to a named person or add conditions. Keep the tone calm and internal, and make the briefing compact enough for the huddle while retaining the relevant figures and context.

Close with a substantive paragraph for the shift leads that brings together the Monday count, the unresolved rice-seal check, the threshold-based restock discussion, and the two separate Wednesday delivery situations. Make clear that the yogurt action depends on the stated confirmation condition and that the apple order remains scheduled separately. Do not imply that either delivery has arrived, recommend or approve an order, decide what happens to the damaged bag, or add a conclusion beyond the notes."}]
